root_cause.text: A race condition exists in `f2fs_compress_write_end_io()` because the `F2FS_WB_CP_DATA` writeback counter is decremented via `dec_page_count()` before the function finishes accessing the `sbi` structure, allowing a concurrent unmount thread to prematurely free `sbi` and destroy `sbi->page_array_slab`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff moves the call to `dec_page_count(sbi, type)` from the beginning of `f2fs_compress_write_end_io()` to the very end of the function, after `page_array_free(sbi, ...)` has executed. The commit message explains that decrementing the counter too early can unblock `f2fs_wait_on_all_pages()` in the concurrent unmount path, leading to the destruction of `sbi->page_array_slab` and `sbi` while `page_array_free()` is still executing and attempting to dereference them.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix page count accounting in f2fs compression write end IO by conditionally decrementing the page count only when pending pages remain.
intent_record.what: The call to dec_page_count is moved inside the conditional block that checks if atomic_dec_return on pending_pages is non-zero.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the page count is only decremented when there are still pending pages remaining, preventing incorrect accounting when the pending count reaches zero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Postpone page count decrement to the end of compression write end I/O to avoid a use-after-free race during unmount.
intent_record.what: Added a call to dec_page_count(sbi, type) along with an explanatory comment at the end of the f2fs_compress_write_end_io function.
intent_record.how: Ensures that decrementing the writeback page counter is the final operation accessing the sbi structure, preventing a race condition where the unmount thread destroys sbi while it is still being accessed.

bic_trace_step.reason: In f2fs_compress_write_end_io(), the writeback counter is decremented via dec_page_count(sbi, F2FS_WB_DATA) on line 1297, before checking if this is the last pending page via atomic_dec_return(&cic->pending_pages) on line 1299. If it is the last page, the function continues to process and free resources using the 'sbi' structure, but a concurrent unmount thread could have already freed 'sbi' because the writeback counter reached zero prematurely.
